extracted.intended_audience: principal investigators, co-PIs, authorized organizational representatives (AORs), sponsored projects offices (SPOs), and institutional officials submitting proposals to NSF
extracted.subtask_description: Official NSF PAPPG guidance on non-award decisions and transactions (withdrawal, return without review, declination, reconsideration, and resubmission) for proposals submitted to the National Science Foundation. Describes processes, timelines, applicability, and institutional responsibilities.

rubrics_metrics.name: Principal Investigator’s Proposal Withdrawal
rubrics_metrics.description: Allows a PI to initiate a proposal withdrawal and forward it to the organization’s AOR for submission to NSF via Research.gov.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Research.gov automates the withdrawal process through the Withdrawals Module. If NSF already has made a funding decision, the proposal cannot be withdrawn electronically and the PI should contact the cognizant NSF Program Officer. Copies of reviews received before a proposal is withdrawn will be provided to the PI.

rubrics_metrics.name: Sponsored Projects Office (SPO) Proposal Withdrawal
rubrics_metrics.description: Allows an authorized individual in the organization’s SPO to initiate a proposal withdrawal and forward it to the AOR for submission to NSF.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: SPO-initiated withdrawals are handled through Research.gov's Withdrawals Module and follow the same constraints as PI-initiated withdrawals (e.g., cannot withdraw after a funding decision has been made electronically).

rubrics_metrics.name: Proposal Submission Duplicate Withdrawal
rubrics_metrics.description: Prevents the AOR from submitting a new proposal if a duplicate (same organization, same title, same PI and co-PIs) was submitted to NSF within the last two weeks prior to the current submission.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If a duplicate is detected, the AOR may either withdraw the previous duplicate proposal and proceed with the new submission, or modify the new proposal so it differs from the previous proposal.

rubrics_metrics.name: Authorized Individuals for Withdrawal
rubrics_metrics.description: Authorized individuals (including AORs and designated SPO staff) can initiate or review a proposal withdrawal using Research.gov functions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Authorized individuals can use the 'Proposal File Updates/Budget Revisions' function in Research.gov to initiate or review withdrawals. AORs also can initiate withdrawals.

rubrics_metrics.name: No Electronic Withdrawal After Funding Decision
rubrics_metrics.description: Proposals for which NSF has already made a funding decision will not be permitted to be withdrawn via the electronic proposal withdrawal system.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When a PI or authorized official attempts to prepare a withdrawal for such a proposal, Research.gov will display a message instructing them to contact the cognizant NSF Program Officer for assistance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Notification Requirement When Funding Is Accepted Elsewhere
rubrics_metrics.description: NSF must be notified if funding for the proposed project is received from another source or sponsor.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If NSF becomes aware that funding for a proposal has been accepted from another sponsor, NSF will send a withdrawal confirmation to the PI and the SPO without waiting for the official withdrawal notification.

rubrics_metrics.name: Collaborative Proposal Withdrawal Effects
rubrics_metrics.description: When a proposal that is part of a collaborative effort is withdrawn, the electronic withdrawal system will withdraw that proposal along with other proposals identified as part of the collaborative effort.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If the remaining organizations determine the project can still proceed, a new collaborative proposal must be submitted. This applies regardless of whether the withdrawing organization is lead or non-lead.

rubrics_metrics.name: Notification of Withdrawal/Return/Declination/Reconsideration
rubrics_metrics.description: NSF provides notice of a withdrawal, return, declination, or reconsideration to both the PI and the SPO.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Copies of reviews received before a proposal is withdrawn will be provided to the PI. PIs and co-PIs may access review information after concurrence of the cognizant Division Director when review information has been released.

rubrics_metrics.name: Proposal Not Accepted or Returned Without Review — Inappropriate for NSF
rubrics_metrics.description: A proposal will not be accepted or will be returned without review if it is inappropriate for funding by the National Science Foundation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: See Chapter I.B for what constitutes inappropriate proposals for NSF funding; such proposals may be returned without review.

rubrics_metrics.name: Proposal Not Accepted — Insufficient Lead-Time
rubrics_metrics.description: A proposal submitted with insufficient lead-time before the activity is scheduled to begin will not be accepted or will be returned without review.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Timeliness is evaluated relative to the proposed start date; insufficient lead-time is grounds for return without review.

rubrics_metrics.name: Proposal Not Accepted — Full Proposal Following 'Not Invited' Preliminary
rubrics_metrics.description: A full proposal submitted by a proposer that received a 'not invited' response to the submission of a preliminary proposal will not be accepted or will be returned without review.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Program-specific solicitation rules about preliminary/full proposal invitations must be followed; submitting a full proposal after a 'not invited' preliminary is a basis for return.

rubrics_metrics.name: Proposal Not Accepted — Duplicate or Substantially Similar to One Under Consideration
rubrics_metrics.description: A proposal that is a duplicate of, or substantially similar to, a proposal already under consideration by NSF from the same submitter will not be accepted or will be returned without review.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Chapter I.G.2 addresses duplicate submissions; submitting substantially similar material concurrently is prohibited and may trigger return.

rubrics_metrics.name: Proposal Not Accepted — Failure to Meet Proposal Preparation Requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: A proposal that does not meet NSF proposal preparation requirements (e.g., page limitations, formatting instructions, electronic submission) as specified in Part I of the PAPPG, the NSF Grants.gov Application Guide, or program solicitation will not be accepted or will be returned without review.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Noncompliance with PAPPG/Grants.gov or solicitation-specific preparation/formatting rules is grounds for return without review.

rubrics_metrics.name: Proposal Not Accepted — Not Responsive to Funding Opportunity
rubrics_metrics.description: A proposal that is not responsive to the NSF funding opportunity will not be accepted or will be returned without review.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Proposals must address the scope and objectives of the announced funding opportunity; lack of responsiveness is a basis for return.

rubrics_metrics.name: Proposal Not Accepted — Missed Deadline
rubrics_metrics.description: A proposal that does not meet an announced proposal deadline date will not be accepted or will be returned without review.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Timely submission by the published deadline is required; late submissions are subject to return without review.

rubrics_metrics.name: Proposal Not Accepted — Previously Reviewed and Declined Without Substantial Revision
rubrics_metrics.description: A proposal that was previously reviewed and declined and has not been substantially revised will not be accepted or will be returned without review.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Resubmissions that do not substantially address prior review concerns may be returned without review (see Chapter IV.E on resubmission requirements).

rubrics_metrics.name: Proposal Not Accepted — Duplicates an Already Awarded Proposal
rubrics_metrics.description: A proposal that duplicates another proposal that was already awarded will not be accepted or will be returned without review.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Submitting material substantially identical to an already-funded project is prohibited and may result in return without review.

rubrics_metrics.name: Proposal Not Accepted — Missing Required Sections
rubrics_metrics.description: A proposal that does not contain each of the required sections of the proposal, as described in Chapter II.D.2, will not be accepted or will be returned without review.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure all required proposal sections are included per Chapter II.D.2; omission of required sections is a basis for return.

rubrics_metrics.name: Declination Communications and Access to Reviews
rubrics_metrics.description: When a proposal is declined, the PI will receive information and an explanation of the reason(s) for declination along with copies of the reviews considered in making the decision.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If the PI is not satisfied, they may request additional information from the Program Officer or Division Director. PIs/co-PIs may access review information after the decision has the concurrence of the cognizant Division Director and all review information has been released.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reconsideration Purpose and Scope
rubrics_metrics.description: Reconsideration aims to ensure NSF's review was fair and reasonable, both substantively and procedurally, and may address procedural errors such as unaccounted-for conflicts of interest or inappropriate consideration of records, information, or rumor.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reconsideration is not adversarial and does not provide a formal hearing. Scientific/technical merits may be examined within the context of budget availability and program priorities. NSF cannot guarantee that reconsideration will result in an award even if error is established.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reconsideration Inapplicability / Exclusions
rubrics_metrics.description: NSF's reconsideration process does not apply to certain decisions or proposal types.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Exclusions include 'discourage' (non-binding) preliminary decisions; proposals for Fellowships, Travel, Planning, RAPID, EAGER, RAISE, SBIR Phase I, STTR Phase I; and proposals returned without review for insufficient lead-time, missed deadline, or failure to meet PAPPG/grants.gov/specific solicitation preparation requirements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Initial Reconsideration Step — Contact Program Officer or Division Director
rubrics_metrics.description: A PI considering reconsideration should first contact the cognizant NSF Program Officer or Division Director for informal clarification; when declined the PI receives verbatim but unattributed copies of ad hoc reviews and the panel summary (if applicable) and a description of the review process.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This informal opportunity to seek further clarification is required before requesting formal reconsideration by higher-level officials.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reconsideration by the Cognizant Assistant Director (AD/Office Head) — Request Requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: If dissatisfied after contacting the Program Officer/Division Director, the PI may request in writing that NSF reconsider its action by the AD/Office Head, only if the PI first sought clarification and the request is received within 90 days after declination or return.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The request should be addressed to the AD/Office Head and explain why the PI believes the declination or return was unwarranted. The AD/Office Head will reconsider fairness and may request additional information or obtain additional reviews subject to standard review procedures and conflict-of-interest rules.

rubrics_metrics.name: AD/Office Head Reconsideration — Decision Timeline
rubrics_metrics.description: The AD/Office Head will furnish the results of the reconsideration, in writing, to the PI within 45 days after the date of the request.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If results cannot be furnished within 45 days, the AD/Office Head will send a written explanation of the need for more time and indicate the expected date for results. If the AD reaffirms the declination/return, the PI's organization may request further reconsideration by the Deputy Director.

rubrics_metrics.name: Further Reconsideration by the Deputy Director — Request Requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: Within 60 days after the AD/Office Head has notified the PI of the reconsideration results, the proposing organization may request further reconsideration by the Deputy Director of NSF.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The request must be in writing, signed by the organization's president or chief executive officer and by the PI, and should explain why an error may have occurred and why the organization is not satisfied with the AD/Office Head reconsideration. The Deputy Director may request additional information or reviews (subject to standard procedures) and may designate an impartial official to conduct the review.

rubrics_metrics.name: Deputy Director Reconsideration — Decision Timeline and Finality
rubrics_metrics.description: The Deputy Director will furnish the results of further reconsideration in writing within 30 days after receiving the request; the decision made by the Deputy Director is final.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If results cannot be furnished within 30 days, the Deputy Director will send a written explanation of the need for more time and indicate when results can be expected. The Deputy Director may designate another NSF official who had no part in the initial review to conduct the reconsideration.

rubrics_metrics.name: No Consideration of Revisions Made After Declination
rubrics_metrics.description: Revisions made to the proposal after declination will not be considered in connection with the original proposal.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A substantially revised proposal may be submitted as a new proposal under standard procedures, but NSF reserves the right to return without review a proposal that is substantially the same as one previously reviewed and declined.

rubrics_metrics.name: Resubmission — Substantial Revision Required
rubrics_metrics.description: A declined proposal may be resubmitted, but only after it has undergone substantial revision.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: NSF programs that accept proposals anytime may have guidelines or moratoria where a declined proposal (or reasonable facsimile by the same PI/co-PIs) is ineligible for resubmission for a specified period. A resubmitted proposal that has not clearly taken into account major comments or concerns from the prior NSF review may be returned without review. The revised proposal will be treated as a new proposal and subject to standard review procedures.
